tex_content.html:
Lemma
[the interior of a joining geodesic stays inside the ball]

↗ lem:dc-ch3-4-2-nomax ↗ lem:dc-ch3-4-2-bridge-ball ↗ lem:dc-ch3-4-2-maxdeduction

1. ch3:4.2With the exponential-inverse package of section 3 and the bridge radius $\delta '$ of section 3: for every continuous intrinsic geodesic $\gamma $ on an open interval $(l,h)\supsetneq [0,1]$ whose endpoints lie within $\beta \le \delta '$ of $p$, which stays inside $B_{\delta '}(p)$ over $[0,1]$, and which is section 3-admissible at every interior time (base reads into $V$, nonzero chart velocity in the flow's ball of initial conditions), the whole open arc stays strictly inside $B_\beta (p)$: $d(p,\gamma (t))<\beta $ for all $t\in (0,1)$.
Proof

\sketch

The distance $h(t)=d(p,\gamma (t))$ is continuous on $[0,1]$ with $h(0),h(1)\le \beta $. If $h$ had an interior local maximum at $t_0$, re-base $\sigma (s)=\gamma (t_0+s)$ (an affine reparametrisation of a geodesic is a geodesic): the metric$\leftrightarrow $radial bridge $F=d^2$ of section 3 turns the local maximum of $h$ into a local maximum of the chart radial functional at $0$, which section 3 forbids. So $h$ has no interior local maximum, and section 3 yields $h<\beta $ on $(0,1)$.

□
